prompt: The session cookie is set with HttpOnly so page scripts can't read it.
why: HttpOnly limits session theft through script.
trap: It helps against XSS, but what it protects is the session.

prompt: On café wifi, someone copies a session cookie sent over plain HTTP and logs in as the user.
why: Cookies sent without HTTPS can be sniffed. Use the Secure flag and HTTPS.
trap: No password was taken; the session was.

prompt: Sessions never expire, so a stolen cookie works for months.
why: Expiry limits how long a stolen session is useful.
trap: It's not about access rights; it's session lifetime.

prompt: The session ID stays the same before and after login.
tells: stays the same before and after login
why: Not rotating the ID on login allows session fixation. Issue a new one.
trap: It's not CSRF; the attacker plants the session.

prompt: Logging out only clears the cookie in the browser; the session still works on the server.
why: Sessions must be invalidated server-side on logout.
trap: It's not a secret leak; it's a session that won't die.

prompt: The session token is in the URL, so it ends up in logs and shared links.
why: Tokens in URLs leak easily. Keep sessions in cookies or headers.
trap: It's a leak, but of the session specifically.
